items.place: Upper Siang, Siang and East Siang districts, Arunachal Pradesh
items.headline: Internet cut in Upper Siang during dam shutdown
items.text: A 36-hour shutdown against the proposed Siang dam began on Monday demanding detainees' release, and internet was suspended in four Upper Siang areas "to curb misinformation", Arunachal Times reports; Chief Minister Pema Khandu said "we are not talking about dam construction at this stage".

photo.alt: A river valley between steep green hills, seen from a bridge.
photo.caption: The Siang valley in Arunachal Pradesh, seen from a bridge. The shutdown covered Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts.

items.place: Torsa Tea Garden, near Jaigaon, north Bengal
items.headline: Bulldozers clear Torsa tea garden protest site
items.text: Bulldozers cleared a 100-day protest site of about 80 families at Torsa Tea Garden in north Bengal on Monday for the proposed Jaigaon land port, and 11 people were detained, The Statesman reports; the families seek rehabilitation, the case is before the Calcutta High Court, and no official response was reported.

photo.alt: A busy shopping street with clothes stalls on the left, an auto-rickshaw and shop signs, and a gate at the far end.
photo.caption: A street in Jaigaon, north Bengal, in 2015. The land port that the Torsa families are being evicted for is planned at Jaigaon.

items.headline: Court says OCI cardholders cannot protest
items.text: The Bombay High Court said on Monday that Overseas Citizen of India cardholders have no right to protest and asked actor Imran Khan, a US citizen detained at a 10 October Mumbai protest, to apologise, Scroll reports; he apologised, and the court kept on hold a notice ordering him to leave India.

photo.alt: An arched gate with Devanagari lettering over a green iron gate, leading to a tree-lined path where a few people walk.
photo.caption: The entrance to August Kranti Maidan, Mumbai, where Imran Khan was detained at a protest on 10 October.

items.headline: Police shoot Andhra suspect, say he fled
items.text: Police in Anantapur district shot a man arrested on Sunday over a chainsaw attack on a schoolgirl, saying they fired in self-defence when he threw stones and tried to flee; he is in serious condition, Scroll reports, and no inquiry has been reported.

photo.alt: A clock tower lit up at night at a busy roundabout, with light trails from traffic.
photo.caption: The clock tower in Anantapur town at night, in 2011.

items.place: Kassala, River Nile and Northern states, Sudan
items.headline: Drone strikes cut power across eastern Sudan
items.text: Drones hit three substations in Kassala and near Merowe on Monday, cutting power, and at least 16 power stations were targeted in a week, Anadolu reports; Sudan's government accuses Ethiopia of involvement, Ethiopia gave no immediate comment, and the RSF generally does not comment.

photo.alt: Rooftops and a street with parked cars in a town, with tall granite domes of mountains behind.
photo.caption: The centre of Kassala, eastern Sudan, with the Taka Mountains behind, in 2008.

items.headline: Sudan law puts journalists at risk, CPJ says
items.text: CPJ said on Monday that a 19 October change to Article 51 of Sudan's Criminal Act, criminalising online or media support for threats to state security, could bring journalists life in prison or death; the journalists' syndicate warned of prosecutions, and the army did not answer CPJ.

photo.alt: A donkey cart beside a dusty street with a painted wall and a white building behind.
photo.caption: A street in Khartoum, Sudan's capital, in 2013.

items.place: Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir al-Balah, Gaza Strip
items.headline: Israeli fire kills five in Gaza, medics say
items.text: Israeli strikes and fire killed five Palestinians on Monday in Gaza City, al-Mawasi, Khan Younis and east of Deir al-Balah, medical sources told Anadolu; Gaza's government media office counts 1,593 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, and no Israeli military comment was reported.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Tents of displaced Palestinians in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, in 2025. One of Monday's deaths was east of Deir al-Balah.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.place: Mrauk-U, Rakhine State, and Loikaw, Kayah State, Myanmar
items.headline: Air strikes hit Myanmar clinic and school
items.text: Military air strikes on Sunday killed at least 12 people in Rakhine State, including a week-old baby at a maternity clinic in Mrauk-U, and three students at a Loikaw school, an armed group, an aid worker and monitors told Reuters; the military government did not immediately respond.

photo.alt: Old stone temples and stupas among green trees and grass, with a few people and cows on a dirt path, under grey clouds.
photo.caption: Temples at Mrauk-U, Rakhine State, in 2017.

items.place: Ashulia, Gazipur and Mirpur, around Dhaka, Bangladesh
items.headline: Garment workers clash with police over wages
items.text: Thousands of garment workers seeking a 30,000-taka minimum wage clashed with police around Dhaka on Monday, with tear gas used and at least 57 arrested and 58 police injured, AFP reports; the government formed a wage board, and the home minister warned of an "iron hand".

photo.alt: A brick embankment road beside wide floodwater under a cloudy sky, with a food cart and a few people.
photo.caption: An embankment road in Ashulia, near Dhaka, in 2007. Ashulia is one of the industrial areas where workers protested.

items.headline: Iran sets execution of two young protesters
items.text: Iran scheduled the execution of Amirhossein Maleki, 20, and Abolfazl Ebrahimi, 18, in Isfahan on 3 November over January's protests, rights groups told ABC News; authorities accuse them of involvement in killing four security personnel, while a defence lawyer says none was charged with murder.

photo.alt: A wide rectangular square with lawns and paths, surrounded by long arcaded buildings.
photo.caption: Naqsh-e Jahan Square in Isfahan, Iran, in 2016.

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. Police say 69 people have been arrested since arson in Pasighat on 23 October; on 2 November a 36-hour shutdown began and internet was suspended in parts of Upper Siang.
focus.alt: A river valley between steep green hills, seen from a bridge.
